item.title: Formulation Architecture and Processing Mechanics of a Sirolimus Self-Emulsifying Oral Liquid Based on Phosal 50 PG and Polysorbate 80
item.description: The technological core of Rapamune oral solution resides in its lipid/surfactant self-emulsifying drug delivery preconcentrate (SEDDS/SMEDDS). Rather than relying on chemical modification to artificially elevate intrinsic aqueous solubility, this system stably dissolves a poorly water-soluble active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) within an oil-phase carrier matrix composed of amphiphilic lipids and surfactants. Upon dilution with water in the gastrointestinal tract or prior to oral administration, it spontaneously disperses to generate a fine colloidal dispersion. This confines sirolimus within nanoscopic micelles or submicron emulsion droplets, thereby thermodynamically circumventing crystalline precipitation.

item.title: Modern Browser Data Sovereignty Dilemma and Defense Breakthrough: Reverse Engineering and Cross-Machine Migration of Chrome App-Bound Encryption (ABE)
item.description:
Testbed: Windows 11 x64 / Google Chrome 154.0.8037.99 ➔ 155.0.8059.40
Core Topics: Windows DPAPI, App-Bound Encryption (ABE), COM Privilege Elevation Interface, Host Sovereignty, Cross-Machine Cookie Migration

Abstract

In traditional endpoint security models, “the owner of the physical machine and operating system is the ultimate sovereign of the system” is a foundational axiom. However, with the evolution of modern browser sandboxing and credential protection mechanisms, application software has begun attempting to defend against “non-privileged and even privileged processes running on the very same host.” App-Bound Encryption (ABE), introduced by Google Chrome starting with version 127, is a prime exemplar of this defensive philosophy.

item.title: Can AI-Restored Iris Photos Fool Iris Recognition?
item.description:
An experimental record of verifying the biometric fidelity of AI image restoration across three iris recognition algorithms.

Origins

I took several macro photos of my own eyes, wanting a nice set of iris close-ups. However, common issues with smartphone macro photography arose—skewed angles, harsh flash glare reflecting across the pupil, and suboptimal resolution. I decided to use AI to restore and enhance the images. Visually, the output looked remarkably impressive to the naked eye.
